description: A two-panel composite of contour (field) maps rendered in a jet-type rainbow scale (dark blue → green → yellow → orange → red). Both panels show the same rhombus / parallelogram silhouette with rounded corners and two sharp opposite points — i.e. a 2D section of a plane-strain-compressed forging specimen, consistent with the multiaxial-forging geometry of the paper. The only annotation is a coordinate triad at the lower right of the group, labelled X (red), Y (green, pointing up) and Z (blue). Left panel: a mostly green field carrying an elongated yellow band running diagonally from the upper-left toward the lower-right point, with dark-blue patches confined to the two pointed corners — a mildly heterogeneous field. Right panel: a large, central red core surrounded by concentric orange, yellow and green bands that follow the rhombus outline — a strongly peaked, near-centrosymmetric field. No panel letters, axis ticks, axis titles, colour bar, scale bar or printed numbers appear anywhere, and no caption was extracted, so the mapped physical quantity (e.g. effective strain/stress from a finite-element simulation, or an EBSD-derived index such as KAM) cannot be identified from the figure itself. The pair supports one argument: the field intensity is much more strongly localised in the right-hand state than in the left-hand one, with the maximum at the centre rather than in a diagonal band.
measured_quantities: spatial distribution of the mapped field quantity (colour scale only, no units printed)

observations.observation: The figure consists of two side-by-side rhombus-shaped contour maps drawn with a jet-like rainbow colour scheme (dark blue, green, yellow, orange, red).
No colour bar, no axis ticks, no axis titles, no scale bar and no printed numeric values are visible in either panel.
A coordinate triad is printed at the lower right, with X shown in red, Y in green pointing upward and Z in blue.
The left panel is dominated by green with a diagonal yellow band between the upper-left and lower-right corners and dark-blue regions at the two sharp corners.
The right panel shows a large central red region surrounded by concentric orange, yellow and green zones, so the mapped maximum is at the specimen centre.
Both panels share the same rhombus outline with rounded corners, indicating the same specimen geometry in two different states.
Neither panel is lettered (a)/(b) and no caption was extracted, so the identity of the mapped quantity cannot be established from the figure.

The paper abstract states that processed samples at 0 pass, 1 pass, 3 pass and 5 pass with 33% normal strain per pass were characterized by XRD and EBSD, but the figure carries no label tying either panel to a specific pass.

The paper abstract reports that XRD analysis confirms a noticeable increase in dislocation density with progressive multiaxial forging; the figure contains no numeric dislocation density to confirm this.

sample_hints: Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel (from paper title; not printed on the figure)

subfigures.description: Rhombus-shaped contour map on a jet colour scale: predominantly green background with a diagonal yellow band running from the upper-left region to the lower-right, and dark-blue patches at the two pointed corners. No colour bar or axes; quantity unmapped.

Rhombus-shaped contour map of the same outline: large red central core enclosed by concentric orange, yellow and green bands hugging the specimen edges. Highest values at the centre, lowest at the border. No colour bar or axes.
Sample/reference axes drawn as arrows: red X, green Y (upwards), blue Z, indicating the orientation convention of the mapped sections.
